\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مزرعه} (mazra'e)}{مزرعه (mazra'e)}]{\fa{مزرعه} (mazra'e) — a farm; a field (of crops)}

\label{lesson:FA-C465-mazrae}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a down payment, then the Persian for to overcharge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مزرعه}}
\textbf{\fa{مزرعه}} (\emph{mazra'e}) — \textquotedblleft{}a farm; a field (of crops)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پدربزرگم} \fa{یک} \fa{مزرعه} \fa{کوچک} \fa{در} \fa{روستا} \fa{دارد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pedarbozorgam yek mazra'e-ye kuchek dar rustâ dârad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My grandfather has a small farm in the village.
\end{quote}

Arabic plural \emph{mazâre'}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mazra'e} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{mazraʿa} (EtymDB), a place where seed is sown.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mazra'e}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mazra'e}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a down payment, then the Persian for to overcharge, then say \emph{mazra'e} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گندم} (gandom)}{گندم (gandom)}]{\fa{گندم} (gandom) — wheat}

\label{lesson:FA-C465-gandom}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to overcharge, then the Persian for a farm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گندم}}
\textbf{\fa{گندم}} (\emph{gandom}) — \textquotedblleft{}wheat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{این} \fa{دشت} \fa{گندم} \fa{میکارند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar in dasht gandom mikârand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
They grow wheat on this plain.
\end{quote}

\emph{Ârd-e gandom} — wheat flour.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gandom} is inherited: EtymDB traces it to a Middle Persian word for wheat.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شالیزار} (shâlizâr)}{شالیزار (shâlizâr)}]{\fa{شالیزار} (shâlizâr) — a rice paddy, a paddy field}

\label{lesson:FA-C465-shalizar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a farm, then the Persian for wheat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شالیزار}}
\textbf{\fa{شالیزار}} (\emph{shâlizâr}) — \textquotedblleft{}a rice paddy, a paddy field\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{شمال} \fa{شالیزارهای} \fa{سبز} \fa{زیادی} \fa{هست}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar shomâl shâlizâr-hâ-ye sabz-e ziyâdi hast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the north there are many green rice paddies.
\end{quote}

\emph{shâli} 'rice in the husk' + \emph{-zâr} 'a place full of'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shâlizâr} is built from \emph{shâli} 'rice in the husk' and the native ending \emph{-zâr} 'a place full of', as in \emph{golzâr} 'a rose garden'. The origin of \emph{shâli} is not settled, and EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a farm, then the Persian for wheat, then say \emph{shâlizâr} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تاکستان} (tâkestân)}{تاکستان (tâkestân)}]{\fa{تاکستان} (tâkestân) — a vineyard}

\label{lesson:FA-C465-takestan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for wheat, then the Persian for a rice paddy.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تاکستان}}
\textbf{\fa{تاکستان}} (\emph{tâkestân}) — \textquotedblleft{}a vineyard\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{پاییز} \fa{در} \fa{تاکستان} \fa{انگور} \fa{میچینند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar pâyiz dar tâkestân angur michinand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In autumn they pick grapes in the vineyard.
\end{quote}

\emph{tâk} 'vine' + \emph{-estân} 'place of'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tâkestân} is a native compound of \emph{tâk} 'vine' and the ending \emph{-estân} 'place of', as in \emph{bimârestân} 'hospital'. EtymDB does not list it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شخم} \fa{زدن} (shokhm zadan)}{شخم زدن (shokhm zadan)}]{\fa{شخم} \fa{زدن} (shokhm zadan) — to plough (US: to plow)}

\label{lesson:FA-C465-shokhm-zadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a rice paddy, then the Persian for a vineyard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شخم} \fa{زدن}}
\textbf{\fa{شخم} \fa{زدن}} (\emph{shokhm zadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to plough (US: to plow)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کشاورز} \fa{زمین} \fa{را} \fa{با} \fa{تراکتور} \fa{شخم} \fa{زد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Keshâvarz zamin râ bâ terâktor shokhm zad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The farmer ploughed the land with a tractor.
\end{quote}

\emph{shokhm} 'ploughing' + \emph{zadan}. Present stem \emph{zan-}: \emph{shokhm mizanad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{shokhm zadan} is built from \emph{shokhm} 'ploughing', whose origin is not settled, and the native verb \emph{zadan} 'to strike'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
